title: _ModelCacheWithCascade.put skips the validation-cache cascade when a key is overwritten in place
description: `_ModelCacheWithCascade.put` detects evicted models by diffing the pre-put key snapshot (`before`) against the post-put key set (`after_keys`) and treating `k not in after_keys` as 'was evicted'. This correctly catches LRU capacity evictions (the evicted key disappears from `_data`), but it MISSES the case where `put` is called with a key that already exists and a *different* `ScoringModel` value. The base `LRUCache.put` overwrites in place (`self._data[key] = value`, lines _lru_cache.py:160-164), so the key remains in `after_keys`; the diff yields no evicted models, and `_ms._invalidate_feature_validation_cache_for(old_model)` is never invoked for the replaced object. Consequently the feature-validation cache in `_model_scorer` retains entries keyed on `id(old_model)` (key shape `(id(scoring_model), contract, schema)`, _model_scorer.py:72/317-321). Those entries are now unreachable garbage that linger until LRU pressure or a full `clear()` removes them — the exact leak the targeted cascade was built to prevent (docstring _model_scorer.py:138-148: 'purge them so the table does not fill with dead id() values'). The method's own docstring (lines 144-147) promises 'every eviction triggers the targeted ... hook', so the in-place-replacement value drop is a contract violation.
evidence: Override put (lines 157-171): `before = dict(self._data); super().put(key, value); after_keys = set(self._data); evicted_models = [v for k, v in before.items() if k not in after_keys]`. For an overwrite of an existing key K, K is in both `before` and `after_keys`, so `evicted_models` is empty even though `before[K]` (the old ScoringModel) was just dropped by base put's `self._data[key] = value`. The validation entries keyed on `id(before[K])` are never invalidated. Tests in tests/test_feature_validation_cache.py (TestValidationCacheCascadeEviction) exercise LRU eviction, targeted invalidation, and full clear, but never the same-key overwrite path, so the gap is untested.
behavior_preservation: Reachability through load_mlflow_model is low because the get-then-put sequence is serialized under _artifact_io_lock(run_id, artifact_path) and same-key callers see a get-hit before reaching put; production therefore rarely (if ever) overwrites a live key with a new object. The defect is a latent contract gap in the general-purpose put method (leak, not wrong result, since a stale id-keyed entry only produces a false get-hit if the reused id ALSO collides on contract+schema). A correct fix would diff on value identity for retained keys (e.g. invalidate when before[k] is not self._data[k]) and add a same-key-overwrite cascade test.
